pairs.difference: A: the green chip sits dead-centre on a flat off-white sheet with an even gap on every side and nothing else in the frame. It reads as a cut-out product shot. B: the teal book is tilted and fills more of the card (box height 0.79), its bookmarks reach toward the right edge, and the wood table runs off every border, the way the real camera and trophy cards are staged.
pairs.fix: Bring the chip closer and tilt it in a 3/4 view so it fills most of the card, with one corner close to the edge. Put it on a coloured sci-fi workbench or circuit surface that runs off the card edges instead of a blank white sheet.

pairs.difference: A: the white helmet is a small, frontal, centred lump on a plain violet gradient with wide empty space around it. Its margin of 0.165 is above the real range. B: the sneakers sit lower in the frame and run nearly edge to edge (margin 0.033). The floor/wall horizon is staged like the real pool and soccer cards.
pairs.fix: Draw the helmet larger and turned in a 3/4 view so it fills about two thirds of the card's height, placed a little below centre. Put it on a surface or a light-burst backdrop that runs off the edges.

pairs.difference: A: the flask is a narrow upright shape in the middle of the card (width 0.51, below the real range). Empty pink wall fills both sides, and a brushed-steel counter cuts the lower left. B: the locker plus its open door fills the width, sits on a floor and wall, and the door swings toward the right edge.
pairs.fix: Draw the flask larger and in a 3/4 view, with a second lab item or a bubbling glow beside it, so the group fills most of the card's width. Drop the empty steel counter.

pairs.difference: A: the plane is banked diagonally, and its wing and tail are cut off by the left and right edges (margin 0). That is the bold, cropped framing of the real cards. B: the UFO is a thin flat ellipse floating in the centre with sky on all sides. It fills only 0.40 of the height, below the real range, so at thumbnail size it reads as a small grey disc.
pairs.fix: Draw the flying saucer much larger, tilted toward the viewer so the dome and the underside both show, and let the rim nearly touch the left and right edges. Have it fill about two thirds of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the red bike fills the frame and the car behind it is cut off by the top and right edges (margin 0), so the hero is pressed up close. B: the lunar rover is small in the middle of a wide crater plain, with the dish antenna sticking up. Occupancy is 0.198, the lowest of the pair, and the grey-on-lavender rover has weak separation from the ground.
pairs.fix: Bring the rover close in a low 3/4 view so its wheels and body fill most of the card's width and reach near the bottom edge. Show less moon ground and make the rover's colours brighter against the background.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket is a slim diagonal in the middle of an empty sky with clouds framing it evenly (width 0.535, below the real range). It is a tidy, fully contained emblem. B: the balloon cluster is big and piled high with overlapping shapes, and the strings trail down toward the bottom edge.
pairs.fix: Draw the rocket bigger and closer, so the nose cone nearly touches the top-right corner and the flame trail runs into the lower-left edge, filling the card on the diagonal.

pairs.difference: A: the column is off-centre, its base is cut off by the bottom edge, and a gold plaque overlaps at the right. This is the cropped, close framing of the real lighthouse and computer cards. B: the rose arch is perfectly symmetric, frontal and centred, with both feet standing whole inside the frame on a striped backdrop.
pairs.fix: Turn the arch to a 3/4 angle and bring it closer, so one side runs off the card edge and the path leads into it from the bottom.

pairs.difference: A: the vault door is pressed close and the wall panel runs off every edge, so the hero dominates. B: the gate is small and centred (occupancy 0.157, margin 0.181, both outside the real range), set back behind a large paved foreground and a big sky. It is symmetric and frontal, which is the generated pattern in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Bring the gate closer and angle it in a 3/4 view so the ironwork fills most of the card. Let a brick pillar be cut off by the edge and show less paving.

pairs.difference: A: the console sits on the same brushed-steel counter as the flask in p03, against a plain blue wall, angled, with the counter edge cutting across the bottom. That staging repeats across the sci-fi cards. B: the claw machine stands as a complete object in a teal room corner and is tall in frame (box height 0.86).
pairs.fix: Draw the control console larger and closer, so the screen and the red button sit near the centre of the card. Replace the bare steel counter and flat wall with a coloured light-burst or a starship interior that runs off the edges.

pairs.difference: A: the chess table sits low in a park scene, with a tree and path filling the top. B: the target is the hero, but the teddy bear next to it competes for attention. Both stay within the real ranges, and on composition alone neither is clearly off.

A: the fan is cropped by the bottom edge (margin 0), with a curtain and wall corner behind it. That is close, cut-off framing like the real lighthouse card. B: the satellite dish stands whole on a grey rooftop against an empty sky. It is narrow (width 0.507) with wide empty margins (0.121), both outside the real range, and much of the card is bare concrete.
pairs.fix: Bring the satellite dish close and tilt the bowl toward the viewer so it fills most of the card. Let the mount be cut off by the bottom edge, and put a colourful sky or a light-burst behind it instead of bare concrete.

pairs.difference: A: the open medal box is big, tilted and fills the card over a light-burst background. B: the satellite is a small, perfectly level, symmetric cross shape floating in the centre of the burst (box height 0.406, well below the real range, occupancy 0.18). At thumbnail size the solar panels shrink to thin slivers.
pairs.fix: Draw the satellite much larger in a tilted 3/4 view, with the solar panels angled toward the viewer and reaching near the left and right edges, so the gold body fills the centre of the card.

pattern: Generated cards stage the hero as a small, complete, centred cut-out with empty background on all sides. They are often frontal or perfectly level and symmetric (UFO, satellite, rover, dish, helmet), or set on a recurring bare steel counter against a plain wall. Real cards bring the object close, tilt it in a 3/4 view, and let it or its setting run off the card edges, so the hero dominates the thumbnail.
